queries: National Audit Office WannaCry NHS could have been prevented basic IT security
nao.org.uk Investigation: WannaCry cyber attack and the NHS summary relatively simple action

sources_considered.why: Primary official source: the UK National Audit Office's press release on its investigation.
Secondary news coverage of the same NAO report. The primary source is enough.

evidence_items.locator: quote from Amyas Morse, head of the NAO

receipt.public_excerpt: It was a relatively unsophisticated attack and could have been prevented by the NHS following basic IT security best practice.

evidence_items.explanation: The head of the UK public spending auditor says the attack was preventable through basic IT security practice, which matches Marcus's claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: all organisations infected by WannaCry shared the same vulnerability and could have taken relatively simple action to protect themselves. Infected organisations had unpatched, or unsupported Windows operating systems so were susceptible to the ransomware.

evidence_items.explanation: Ties the infections to local failures to patch or manage firewalls, which is the 'keeping up on cybersecurity procedures' Marcus describes.

receipt.public_excerpt: In March and April 2017, NHS Digital had issued critical alerts warning organisations to patch their systems to prevent WannaCry. However, before 12 May 2017, the Department had no formal mechanism for assessing whether local NHS organisations had complied

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms patch alerts were issued before the attack. It also shows the NAO placed some blame on central oversight, not only on local hospitals.
